title: POC weekly - quality drift & guardrail investigation with Cliffside Care
summary: Weekly POC sync to investigate recent quality drift on triage prompts. We reviewed scorecard deltas, identified 3 prompt permutations that regressed after a model swap, discussed guardrail tightening and monitoring thresholds, and agreed on next steps: run isolation A/B for model variants, share security artifacts, and schedule a focused evaluation run with 5k prompts.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-11
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM), Nina (Cliffside Head of Data), Marcus (ML Eng), Aisha (PM), Tom (Security)
---
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, quick roll call. we got nina, marcus, aisha, tom on the cusp?
[00:06] Nina: yep here, hi.
[00:07] Marcus: here.
[00:08] Aisha: hi all.
[00:10] Maya: great. ok quick objective for today is to walk through the scorecard deltas you saw yesterday and dig into a couple of prompt regressions, and then decide whether to tighten the guardrails or roll back to the earlier model variant.
[00:22] Diego: i'll share my screen, i pulled the batch eval from friday — you'll see baseline v12 vs v13, and there's a clear dip in Recall@top1 for the diagnosis prompts. weirdly precision held up.
[00:35] Nina: yeah our ops alert fired, about a 6.8% drop in top-1 accuracy on the triage set. not catastrophic but it's above our threshold.
[00:43] Marcus: quick context — we switched to a quantized variant last week to save token cost, that was supposed to be nearly indistinguishable.
[00:52] Diego: right, and the quantization profile used reduced FP bits and a different kernel which may affect conditional probabilities for short completions. the KV cache behavior looked fine, though — or at least the logs don't show cache misses. app logs say some answer truncation happened, odd.
[01:10] Aisha: do we have an example prompt that regressed? we want something we can point product at.
[01:14] Maya: yes, diego — can you read through the 3 failing prompts?
[01:18] Diego: sure. first one: "Patient presents with chest pain, ECG normal, what next?" baseline answer was stepwise — order troponin and monitor for four hours; new model gave a general reassurance and suggested outpatient follow-up which is wrong for our triage bar.
[01:35] Marcus: that is exactly the case we flagged. it's dangerous because the user-facing assistant may under-escalate.
[01:41] Tom: and from sec standpoint, we need deterministic guardrails to prevent under-escalation. if the model variance increases risk, we must mitigate.
[01:50] Nina: side question — did the model swap also change temperature or stopping heuristics? our config shows temperature 0.0 but maybe the token stop sequence handling changed?
[01:59] Diego: good point, we did disable some stop-sequence postprocessing in the runtime to test streaming behavior. that could be related. i should add that to the matrix.
[02:08] Maya: ok so potential causes on the table: quantization effect, kernel selection differences, and stop-sequence/streaming config.
[02:16] Priya: also noting the eval scoring — the heatmap shows drift concentrated in short-answer clinical prompts rather than long narrative ones. so prompts that expect a single recommendation are more sensitive.
[02:28] [02:28] Marcus: can we run an isolation A/B — pin baseline weights on 50% of traffic for 24 hours? we want to compare real traffic not just synthetic.
[02:36] Maya: yes we can do a traffic split. for the POC we can do rollout policy canary with 10/90 up to 50/50, but we need to discuss capacity if you're worried about latencies.
[02:46] Nina: latencies are fine; our concern is correctness. cost savings were attractive, but not at patient-safety risk.
[02:53] Diego: i'll flag one more thing — the internal reranker that we added for answer selection might behave differently post-quant. it's small but could change top-1 picks.
[03:03] Aisha: is the reranker part of Redwood's managed pipeline or our side? it's in our pipeline right now but uses embeddings from the Redwood endpoint.
[03:11] Maya: correct, you're using our embed endpoint then doing a rerank client-side. we did see an embedding cosine shift of 0.02 on average between the variants. small but could cause reorderings.
[03:22] Tom: security question — if we roll back the model will we incur extra cost or is there versioning penalties? also need to get KMS logs for the traffic in question.
[03:32] Diego: no versioning penalty; we keep model variants available. regarding KMS logs, we can export key usage, but remember if you're on the hosted plan some logs are redacted; for Private VPC we provide more detailed HSM/KMS audit trails.
[03:46] Nina: cliffside is evaluating private vs dedicated — what was the recommended path again?
[03:50] Maya: for production patient-data sensitive flows we usually recommend Redwood Private (VPC) if you need full control and unredacted audit logs; Dedicated works for high throughput with predictable latency and is SLA-backed. there was a small stutter in the transcript where people called it Redwood Privy — that's a common transcription hiccup.
[04:06] [04:06] Marcus: back to scoring, we noticed the scorer's threshold for safety flagging didn't fire for those regressed examples. the threshold was set at 0.7 but the new model produced an answer with 0.65 safety score — just below.
[04:20] Diego: we can adjust the scorer to be more conservative — move threshold to 0.75 — but that'll increase false positives. tradeoff between recall of unsafe answers and user friction.
[04:30] Aisha: product-wise we'd prefer higher recall on safety flags, we can tune UI to provide escalation steps rather than block users entirely.
[04:37] Priya: operationally, if we tighten guardrails we should add a monitoring alert for false-positive rate so we don't degrade UX unnoticed.
[04:45] Maya: agree. action plan proposal: 1) run 24h A/B with baseline pinned at 50% to measure real traffic regression, 2) run offline isolation eval on 5k recent prompts with both models, 3) increase safety threshold to 0.75 in a canary to measure FP rate, 4) share security artifacts.
[05:05] Nina: that sounds good. what about timeline for the 5k run? can you do it by end of week?
[05:10] Diego: yes i can spin it up tomorrow; should finish within 36 hours given our batch infrastructure. i'll push results to the shared spreadsheet and link in slack.
[05:19] Maya: ok i'll send a small email to confirm the rollout window for the canary.
[05:23] Marcus: also a note, some prompts show hallucinated recommendations referencing tools we don't integrate. it's subtle, probably because of the model variant's broader completion distribution.
[05:33] Priya: we've also got one regression where the model truncates the last token on streaming — transcript shows 'monitor for four hour' missing trailing s — likely stop-seq/streaming mismatch.
[05:44] Diego: yep that's the stop-sequence thing i mentioned; i'll re-enable the post-processing stop handler for streaming and test.
[05:51] Tom: for security, we'll need the SOC2 package and key rotation logs before we move to dedicated or private. can you share those docs?
[05:59] Maya: yes i will upload the SOC2 attestation and the KMS integration guide to the shared drive. note that the hosted plan redacts some parts, but for Dedicated/Private we can supply the full package.
[06:12] Aisha: what's the impact on latency if we bump safety scoring or add extra reranking?
[06:17] Diego: extra reranking adds 20-40ms on average per request if it's local, if you run it as an additional call to the embed endpoint it could add 80-120ms. for patient triage we still meet sub-400ms SLO in Dedicated; hosted can be higher variance.
[06:34] Nina: ok we need to see a cost estimate for the 50/50 canary and for keeping quantized variant in production vs baseline weights.
[06:41] Maya: i'll include a cost delta in the follow-up email — approximate numbers for token cost difference and the Dedicated delta if relevant.
[06:47] Priya: quick note on evaluation metrics — let's also look at Rouge-L for narrative prompts and exact-match for triage answers so we capture both flavors.
[06:57] Diego: noted. i'll add those metrics to the spreadsheet.
[07:02] Maya: any other blockers?
[07:05] Marcus: none from eng, just want the A/B and the 5k offline run.
[07:09] Nina: same.
[07:11] Maya: ok recap and owners now.
[07:15] [07:15] Diego: (owner) run 5k offline eval and post results to sheet (due 2025-06-13).
[07:22] Maya: (owner) send rollout window and cost delta + SOC2/KMS docs (due 2025-06-12).
[07:28] Priya: (owner) add FP/TP alert to monitoring for safety flags and baseline metrics (due 2025-06-16).
[07:34] Marcus: (owner) confirm client-side reranker logs and share a small sample for debugging (due 2025-06-13).
[07:41] Tom: (owner) send list of required audit logs we need for Private evaluation (due 2025-06-14).
[07:46] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll reconvene after the offline run and the first 24h canary. any final Qs?
[07:52] Aisha: none, thanks.
[07:54] Maya: bye everyone.
[07:56] [end]
action_items: Diego Alvarez (SE): run 5k offline eval and post results to shared spreadsheet (due 2025-06-13)
Maya Chen (AE): send rollout window, cost delta, and SOC2/KMS docs (due 2025-06-12)
Priya Sinha (CSM): add false-positive/true-positive alerts to monitoring and baseline metrics (due 2025-06-16)
Marcus Lee (ML Eng): export client-side reranker logs sample for debugging (due 2025-06-13)
Tom O'Neill (Security): provide list of required audit logs for Private eval (due 2025-06-14)
next_steps: Start 24h A/B canary with baseline pinned at 50% for real-traffic comparison
Run isolated 5k prompt evaluation across both model variants and share scorecard
Canary increase safety threshold to 0.75 in a controlled rollout to measure FP impact
Share SOC2 attestation and KMS/HSM audit guide; confirm Dedicated vs Private checklist
